selected_evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; service active with correct unit config; /health and /inventory endpoints respond; oom_score_adj confirmed -1000

selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving while a memory hog drives the system OOM, and the hog is the process the kernel stops
selected_evidence.summary: memhog launched with default oom_score_adj=0; dmesg shows kernel OOM killer invoked and killed pid 2511 (memhog, oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api pid 2449 (oom_score_adj:-1000) was spared; post-event curl to /health and /inventory succeeded with continuous uptime, proving the service never stopped serving

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot (2s delayed) returned command acknowledgement immediately, before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of inventory-api and OOM protection

commands.command:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory API service
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/inventory-api/app.py
Restart=always
RestartSec=1
# Protect this service from the kernel OOM killer: -1000 disables OOM killing for its processes.
OOMScoreAdjust=-1000
OOMPolicy=continue
NoNewPrivileges=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now inventory-api
sleep 1
systemctl is-active inventory-api
systemctl status inventory-api --no-pager | head -15
